proof_attempt_summary: Angle 0 was abandoned after its conditional modulus remained dependent on arbitrary regular-conditional-law versions. Angle 1 derived the matched rare-cohort rate and boundary classifications in a fixed known-coarsening model, but the field-tier gate stopped at D0.5 because arbitrary-design optimality and broader nuisance robustness remain open. The math referee passed; the decision referee left literature and citation-positioning findings unresolved, and no Lean formalization began.
tldr: Under prespecified inspection laws, fixed known censoring-survival primitives \(G^0_{ax}\), a common known treatment design, and finite strata, conditioning on the realized survey design produces an explicit finite product experiment. For each fixed \(t_0>0\), an empirical current-status average plus an exactly unbiased cohort correction yields finite-sample conditional coverage and matched conditional and unconditional rates \(\min\{n^{-1/3},(nm)^{-1/4}\}\) in the nondegenerate density-envelope branch, with crossover at \(m=n^{1/3}\). Separate classifications give root-\(n\) behavior in the nonsaturated known-slope interior branch and zero risk at support-anchored or saturated-mass boundaries. No universal optimality claim is made for arbitrary irregular realized designs.
gap: Published current-status intervals can guarantee coverage conditional on assessment times, but they use one coarsening channel and do not characterize conditional expected length after an independent right-censored source is added. Published mixed-source inference uses fixed-fraction asymptotics and does not condition its guarantee on the realized survey schedule.
fill: Under a prespecified inspection mechanism, fixed known censoring-survival primitives \(G^0_{ax}\), and an explicit common-propensity design restriction, the empirical-design correction, one observable conditional Bernstein interval over the entire law class, same-experiment triangular converse, typical-design unconditional consequence, and all-design modulus question separate coverage for every schedule from optimal length on typical and irregular schedules.
